records.source: וַיַּ֣רְא יַעֲקֹ֔ב כִּ֥י יֶשׁ־שֶׁ֖בֶר בְּמִצְרָ֑יִם וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יַעֲקֹב֙ לְבָנָ֔יו לָ֖מָּה תִּתְרָאֽוּ׃
records.gloss: And saw Jacob that there [was] grain in Egypt, and said Jacob to his sons, why do you look at one another?
pieces: Jacob saw that grain was to be had in Egypt, and he asked his sons, "Why do you keep staring at one another?"

L.1: And Jacob saw that there was grain in Egypt, and Jacob said to his sons, "Why do you look at one another?"

R.1: Jacob learned that people could get grain in Egypt. He said to his sons, "Why do you sit and stare at each other?"

decisions.choice: Jacob saw: he learned
decisions.reason: "Saw" here means came to know; verse 2 says he had heard it.

decisions.choice: grain: grain for sale
decisions.reason: Shever is grain as it was bought and sold, related to the verb shavar, "buy grain" (verse 2; 41:56). The two words run through chapters 41-44.

decisions.choice: why do you look at one another?: why do you do nothing?
decisions.reason: Jacob rebukes his sons for standing around, each waiting for another to act, while the family goes hungry.

records.source: וַיֹּ֕אמֶר הִנֵּ֣ה שָׁמַ֔עְתִּי כִּ֥י יֶשׁ־שֶׁ֖בֶר בְּמִצְרָ֑יִם רְדוּ־שָׁ֨מָּה֙ וְשִׁבְרוּ־לָ֣נוּ מִשָּׁ֔ם וְנִחְיֶ֖ה וְלֹ֥א נָמֽוּת׃
records.gloss: And he said, behold, I have heard that there is grain in Egypt; go down there and buy grain for us from there, that we may live and not die.
pieces: He said, "I am told there is grain in Egypt. Go down there and buy us grain, so that we stay alive and do not die."

L.2: And he said, "Look, I have heard that there is grain in Egypt. Go down there and buy [grain] for us from there, so that we may live and not die."

R.2: He said, "People tell me there is grain in Egypt. Go and get us some there, so we can stay alive. Otherwise we will die."

decisions.choice: go down: Egypt lies below Canaan
decisions.reason: One "goes down" to Egypt from the hill country of Canaan and "goes up" from it (12:10; 13:1). The words also fit the story's other descents: Joseph went down into the pit and into Egypt (37:25; 39:1).

decisions.choice: that we may live and not die
decisions.reason: The words come back when Judah urges Jacob to let Benjamin go (43:8). Joseph later sees God at work to keep the family alive (45:5, 7).

records.source: וַיֵּרְד֥וּ אֲחֵֽי־יוֹסֵ֖ף עֲשָׂרָ֑ה לִשְׁבֹּ֥ר בָּ֖ר מִמִּצְרָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: And went down [the] brothers of Joseph, ten, to buy grain from Egypt.
pieces: Ten of Joseph's brothers set off down to Egypt for grain.

L.3: So Joseph's ten brothers went down to buy grain from Egypt.

R.3: So ten of Joseph's brothers set out for Egypt to get grain.

decisions.choice: Joseph's brothers: named by their tie to Joseph
decisions.reason: The narrator calls them "Joseph's brothers" though they do not know they will meet him; the reader is reminded who is waiting in Egypt. In verse 5 they are "the sons of Israel".

records.source: וְאֶת־בִּנְיָמִין֙ אֲחִ֣י יוֹסֵ֔ף לֹא־שָׁלַ֥ח יַעֲקֹ֖ב אֶת־אֶחָ֑יו כִּ֣י אָמַ֔ר פֶּן־יִקְרָאֶ֖נּוּ אָסֽוֹן׃
records.gloss: But Benjamin, [the] brother of Joseph, not did send Jacob with his brothers, for he said, lest befall him harm.
pieces: But Jacob kept Benjamin, Joseph's brother, at home and did not send him with the others, because he was afraid something might happen to him.

L.4: But Jacob did not send Benjamin, Joseph's brother, with his brothers, for he said, "Harm might come to him."

R.4: Jacob would not let Benjamin, Joseph's brother, go with them. He feared that Benjamin might get hurt.

decisions.choice: Benjamin, Joseph's brother: the other son of Rachel
decisions.reason: All the brothers were Joseph's brothers, but only Benjamin had the same mother, Rachel (35:18, 24). Jacob now favors him as he once favored Joseph.

decisions.choice: harm: a fatal accident or disaster
decisions.reason: Ason is serious harm, often deadly (Exodus 21:22-23). Jacob uses the word again in verse 38 and 44:29.

records.source: וַיָּבֹ֨אוּ֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לִשְׁבֹּ֖ר בְּת֣וֹךְ הַבָּאִ֑ים כִּֽי־הָיָ֥ה הָרָעָ֖ב בְּאֶ֥רֶץ כְּנָֽעַן׃
records.gloss: And came [the] sons of Israel to buy grain among those coming, for was the famine in [the] land of Canaan.
pieces: The sons of Israel came to buy grain along with everyone else who was coming, because the famine had reached the land of Canaan.

L.5: And the sons of Israel came to buy grain among those who came, for the famine was in the land of Canaan.

R.5: Many people were going to Egypt to buy grain, and Israel's sons went along with them, because the famine was in Canaan as well.

decisions.choice: the sons of Israel: Jacob's sons
decisions.reason: Israel is Jacob's God-given name (32:28). The phrase that later names the whole people here still means his own sons, the fathers of the tribes.

records.source: וְיוֹסֵ֗ף ה֚וּא הַשַּׁלִּ֣יט עַל־הָאָ֔רֶץ ה֥וּא הַמַּשְׁבִּ֖יר לְכָל־עַ֣ם הָאָ֑רֶץ וַיָּבֹ֨אוּ֙ אֲחֵ֣י יוֹסֵ֔ף וַיִּשְׁתַּֽחֲווּ־ל֥וֹ אַפַּ֖יִם אָֽרְצָה׃
records.gloss: And Joseph, he [was] the ruler over the land; he [was] the one selling grain to all [the] people of the land. And came [the] brothers of Joseph and bowed down to him, face to [the] ground.
pieces: Joseph was the man in power over the country, and he oversaw the sale of grain to all its people. Joseph's brothers came in and bowed low before him, their faces to the ground.

L.6: Now Joseph, he [was] the ruler over the land; he [was] the one who sold grain to all the people of the land. And Joseph's brothers came and bowed down to him with [their] faces to the ground.

R.6: Joseph ruled over Egypt, and all the people bought their grain from him. So when his brothers arrived, they knelt in front of him and put their faces down to the ground.

decisions.choice: the ruler: the one holding power
decisions.reason: Shallit means one who has authority or mastery. It describes Joseph's place under Pharaoh (41:40-44).

decisions.choice: bowed down to him: Joseph's dream comes true
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used in Joseph's dream of the sheaves bowing to his sheaf (37:7). The brothers who mocked the dream now fulfill it without knowing.

records.source: וַיַּ֥רְא יוֹסֵ֛ף אֶת־אֶחָ֖יו וַיַּכִּרֵ֑ם וַיִּתְנַכֵּ֨ר אֲלֵיהֶ֜ם וַיְדַבֵּ֧ר אִתָּ֣ם קָשׁ֗וֹת וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֲלֵהֶם֙ מֵאַ֣יִן בָּאתֶ֔ם וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ מֵאֶ֥רֶץ כְּנַ֖עַן לִשְׁבָּר־אֹֽכֶל׃
records.gloss: And saw Joseph his brothers and recognized them, and he made himself a stranger to them and spoke with them harsh [things], and said to them, from where have you come? And they said, from [the] land of Canaan to buy food.
pieces: Joseph knew his brothers the moment he saw them, but he treated them like strangers and spoke to them sternly. He demanded, "Where have you come from?" They said, "We have come from Canaan to buy food."

L.7: And Joseph saw his brothers and recognized them, but he made himself a stranger to them and spoke harshly with them. And he said to them, "Where have you come from?" And they said, "From the land of Canaan, to buy food."

R.7: Joseph knew his brothers as soon as he saw them. But he spoke to them roughly, as if they were strangers to him. "Where are you from?" he asked. They said, "We have come from Canaan to buy food."

decisions.choice: recognized ... made himself a stranger: a play on one root
decisions.reason: Both verbs come from the root nkr. Joseph "recognized" them (hikkir) and "made himself unrecognizable" (hitnakker). The same root marked the brothers' deceit, "examine (hakker) whether this is your son's robe" (37:32), and Judah's exposure (38:25-26).

records.source: וַיַּכֵּ֥ר יוֹסֵ֖ף אֶת־אֶחָ֑יו וְהֵ֖ם לֹ֥א הִכִּרֻֽהוּ׃
records.gloss: And recognized Joseph his brothers, but they not recognized him.
pieces: Joseph knew his brothers, but they had no idea who he was.

L.8: And Joseph recognized his brothers, but they did not recognize him.

R.8: Joseph knew who his brothers were, but they did not know who he was.

decisions.choice: they did not recognize him: a grown man in Egyptian dress
decisions.reason: Joseph was seventeen when they sold him and is now near forty. He is clean-shaven like an Egyptian (41:14), dressed as a high official, and speaks to them through an interpreter (verse 23).

records.source: וַיִּזְכֹּ֣ר יוֹסֵ֔ף אֵ֚ת הַחֲלֹמ֔וֹת אֲשֶׁ֥ר חָלַ֖ם לָהֶ֑ם וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֲלֵהֶם֙ מְרַגְּלִ֣ים אַתֶּ֔ם לִרְא֛וֹת אֶת־עֶרְוַ֥ת הָאָ֖רֶץ בָּאתֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And remembered Joseph the dreams which he had dreamed about them, and he said to them, spies you [are]; to see [the] nakedness of the land you have come.
pieces: Joseph called to mind the dreams he had dreamed about them. "You are spies," he told them. "You came to look for the weak spots in our country's defenses."

L.9: And Joseph remembered the dreams that he had dreamed about them, and he said to them, "You are spies! You have come to see the nakedness of the land."

R.9: Joseph thought back to the dreams he had had about them. "You are spies!" he said. "You want to find the weak places in our country so you can attack it."

decisions.choice: he remembered the dreams: the sheaves and the stars
decisions.reason: Seeing his brothers bow to the ground (verse 6) brings back the dreams of 37:5-10.

decisions.choice: the nakedness of the land: its undefended places
decisions.reason: "Nakedness" (ervah) is what is exposed and unprotected. Spies would look for the places where a country could be attacked. Egypt guarded its northeastern frontier against intruders from Canaan, so the charge was plausible.

decisions.choice: so you can attack it
decisions.reason: Readable spells out why spies would look for weak places.

records.source: וַיֹּאמְר֥וּ אֵלָ֖יו לֹ֣א אֲדֹנִ֑י וַעֲבָדֶ֥יךָ בָּ֖אוּ לִשְׁבָּר־אֹֽכֶל׃
records.gloss: And they said to him, no, my lord; and your servants have come to buy food.
pieces: "Not at all, my lord," they protested. "Your servants have come for nothing but food.

L.10: And they said to him, "No, my lord! Your servants have come to buy food.

R.10: They answered, "No, sir! We have come only to buy food.

decisions.choice: my lord ... your servants: polite speech before a ruler
decisions.reason: The brothers call Joseph "my lord" and themselves "your servants", the humble courtesy of people before a great man (44:7, 19). Without knowing it they speak the words of Joseph's dreams.

decisions.choice: sir ... we
decisions.reason: Readable uses "sir" and "we", as in chapter 44.

records.source: כֻּלָּ֕נוּ בְּנֵ֥י אִישׁ־אֶחָ֖ד נָ֑חְנוּ כֵּנִ֣ים אֲנַ֔חְנוּ לֹא־הָי֥וּ עֲבָדֶ֖יךָ מְרַגְּלִֽים׃
records.gloss: All of us, sons of one man we [are]; honest we [are]; not are your servants spies.
pieces: We are all brothers, sons of one father, and we are honest men. Your servants are no spies."

L.11: We are all sons of one man. We are honest [men]; your servants are not spies."

R.11: We are all brothers, with one father. We are honest men. We are not here to spy."

decisions.choice: sons of one man: a family, not a band of spies
decisions.reason: Ten brothers traveling together are plainly one family. No father would risk all his sons together on a spying mission.

decisions.choice: honest: upright, truthful
decisions.reason: Kenim means right, true, honest. The word runs through the chapter (verses 19, 31, 33, 34). The brothers who lied to their father about Joseph insist on their honesty.

records.source: וַיֹּ֖אמֶר אֲלֵהֶ֑ם לֹ֕א כִּֽי־עֶרְוַ֥ת הָאָ֖רֶץ בָּאתֶ֥ם לִרְאֽוֹת׃
records.gloss: And he said to them, no, for [the] nakedness of the land you have come to see.
pieces: "Not so," he told them. "You have come to spy out where the land is unguarded."

L.12: And he said to them, "No, you have come to see the nakedness of the land!"

R.12: But Joseph told them, "That is not true. You came to find our country's weak places."

records.source: וַיֹּאמְר֗וּ שְׁנֵ֣ים עָשָׂר֩ עֲבָדֶ֨יךָ אַחִ֧ים׀אֲנַ֛חְנוּ בְּנֵ֥י אִישׁ־אֶחָ֖ד בְּאֶ֣רֶץ כְּנָ֑עַן וְהִנֵּ֨ה הַקָּטֹ֤ן אֶת־אָבִ֨ינוּ֙ הַיּ֔וֹם וְהָאֶחָ֖ד אֵינֶֽנּוּ׃
records.gloss: And they said, twelve your servants [are], brothers we [are], sons of one man in [the] land of Canaan; and behold, the youngest [is] with our father today, and the one is not.
pieces: They answered, "There are twelve of us, your servants, all brothers, sons of one man in the land of Canaan. The youngest is at home with our father just now, and one brother is gone."

L.13: And they said, "Your servants are twelve brothers, the sons of one man in the land of Canaan. And look, the youngest is with our father today, and one is no more."

R.13: They said, "There are twelve of us brothers. We all have the same father, and he lives in Canaan. Our youngest brother is at home with him now, and one of our brothers is gone."

decisions.choice: one is not: one is gone, dead
decisions.reason: "He is not" is a way of saying someone has vanished or died (5:24; 37:30; 42:36). The brother who "is not" is the man they are speaking to.

decisions.choice: the youngest: the brothers give Joseph what he wants to know
decisions.reason: In defending themselves the brothers tell Joseph, without being asked, that his father is alive and that Benjamin is safe at home.

records.source: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר אֲלֵהֶ֖ם יוֹסֵ֑ף ה֗וּא אֲשֶׁ֨ר דִּבַּ֧רְתִּי אֲלֵכֶ֛ם לֵאמֹ֖ר מְרַגְּלִ֥ים אַתֶּֽם׃
records.gloss: And said to them Joseph, it [is] what I said to you, saying, spies you [are].
pieces: "It is exactly what I said," Joseph told them. "You are spies.

L.14: And Joseph said to them, "It is just as I said to you: you are spies!

R.14: Joseph said to them, "I was right. You are spies!

records.source: בְּזֹ֖את תִּבָּחֵ֑נוּ חֵ֤י פַרְעֹה֙ אִם־תֵּצְא֣וּ מִזֶּ֔ה כִּ֧י אִם־בְּב֛וֹא אֲחִיכֶ֥ם הַקָּטֹ֖ן הֵֽנָּה׃
records.gloss: By this you will be tested: [by the] life of Pharaoh, you will not go out from here unless comes your youngest brother here.
pieces: Here is how I will test you. I swear by Pharaoh's life that you will not get out of here until your youngest brother shows up.

L.15: By this you shall be tested: by the life of Pharaoh, you shall not leave this place unless your youngest brother comes here.

R.15: So I am going to test you. I swear by the life of Pharaoh, you will stay here until your youngest brother comes.

decisions.choice: tested: put to the proof
decisions.reason: Bachan means to test, as metal is tried to see if it is pure (Jeremiah 9:7). The brothers' words will be tested, and so will they themselves.

decisions.choice: by the life of Pharaoh: an Egyptian oath
decisions.reason: Joseph swears as an Egyptian official would, by the king's life, keeping up his disguise.

records.source: שִׁלְח֨וּ מִכֶּ֣ם אֶחָד֮ וְיִקַּ֣ח אֶת־אֲחִיכֶם֒ וְאַתֶּם֙ הֵאָ֣סְר֔וּ וְיִבָּֽחֲנוּ֙ דִּבְרֵיכֶ֔ם הַֽאֱמֶ֖ת אִתְּכֶ֑ם וְאִם־לֹ֕א חֵ֣י פַרְעֹ֔ה כִּ֥י מְרַגְּלִ֖ים אַתֶּֽם׃
records.gloss: Send from you one, and let him get your brother, and you, be imprisoned, that may be tested your words, whether truth [is] with you; and if not, [by the] life of Pharaoh, surely spies you [are].
pieces: Pick one of you to go and bring your brother back, and the others will be held in prison. Then we will find out whether there is any truth in what you say. If there is not, I swear by Pharaoh's life, you are spies!"

L.16: Send one of you, and let him get your brother, while you are kept in prison, so that your words may be tested, whether there is truth in you. And if not, by the life of Pharaoh, surely you are spies!"

R.16: One of you can go back and bring your brother here. The others will be kept in prison. Then we will see if what you say is true. If it is not, I swear by the life of Pharaoh that you are spies!"

records.source: וַיֶּאֱסֹ֥ף אֹתָ֛ם אֶל־מִשְׁמָ֖ר שְׁלֹ֥שֶׁת יָמִֽים׃
records.gloss: And he put them together into custody three days.
pieces: Then he locked them all up together for three days.

L.17: And he put them all together in custody for three days.

R.17: Joseph had them all put in prison, and they stayed there three days.

decisions.choice: custody: the brothers taste Joseph's confinement
decisions.reason: Mishmar, "custody", is the word for the place where Joseph was held with Pharaoh's officials (40:3-4; 41:10). For three days the brothers are prisoners, as he was for years.

records.source: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֲלֵהֶ֤ם יוֹסֵף֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשְּׁלִישִׁ֔י זֹ֥את עֲשׂ֖וּ וִֽחְי֑וּ אֶת־הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים אֲנִ֥י יָרֵֽא׃
records.gloss: And said to them Joseph on the day the third, this do and live; God I fear.
pieces: On the third day Joseph told them, "I am a God-fearing man, so if you do what I say, you will live.

L.18: And Joseph said to them on the third day, "Do this and live, [for] I fear God.

R.18: On the third day Joseph said to them, "I am a man who honors God. Do what I tell you, and you will stay alive.

decisions.choice: I fear God: a man who will deal justly
decisions.reason: To "fear God" is to revere him and so act rightly toward others (20:11; 22:12). The brothers, who expected nothing from a foreign ruler, hear him speak of "God", the God they themselves worship.

records.source: אִם־כֵּנִ֣ים אַתֶּ֔ם אֲחִיכֶ֣ם אֶחָ֔ד יֵאָסֵ֖ר בְּבֵ֣ית מִשְׁמַרְכֶ֑ם וְאַתֶּם֙ לְכ֣וּ הָבִ֔יאוּ שֶׁ֖בֶר רַעֲב֥וֹן בָּתֵּיכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: If honest you [are], your brother, one, let him be confined in [the] house of your custody, and you, go, carry grain for [the] hunger of your households.
pieces: If you are as honest as you say, let one of your brothers stay locked up where you have been held, and the others may go and carry grain home to feed your hungry families.

L.19: If you are honest [men], let one of your brothers be confined in the house where you are in custody, and the rest of you go [and] carry grain for the hunger of your households.

R.19: If you are honest, leave one of your brothers here in prison. The rest of you may take grain back to your families, who are hungry.

decisions.choice: grain for the hunger of your households: food for your starving families
decisions.reason: "The hunger of your households" means the families at home who are going hungry. Joseph's first change of plan (verse 16) shows his concern for them.

records.source: וְאֶת־אֲחִיכֶ֤ם הַקָּטֹן֙ תָּבִ֣יאוּ אֵלַ֔י וְיֵאָמְנ֥וּ דִבְרֵיכֶ֖ם וְלֹ֣א תָמ֑וּתוּ וַיַּעֲשׂוּ־כֵֽן׃
records.gloss: And your brother, the youngest, you will bring to me, that may be verified your words and you will not die. And they did so.
pieces: Then bring your youngest brother to me. That way what you have said will be proved true, and you will not have to die." And they agreed to this.

L.20: And bring your youngest brother to me, so that your words may be confirmed and you will not die." And they did so.

R.20: Then come back with your youngest brother. That will prove you were telling the truth, and you will not die." The brothers agreed to do this.

decisions.choice: confirmed: shown to be true
decisions.reason: The verb is from aman, "be firm, reliable", the root of "amen" and of the word for faith (15:6). Their words must prove trustworthy.

decisions.choice: they did so: they agreed, or began to do it
alternatives: they carried it out at once
decisions.reason: The return trip comes much later. "They did so" probably means they accepted the terms and began preparing to leave.

records.source: וַיֹּאמְר֞וּ אִ֣ישׁ אֶל־אָחִ֗יו אֲבָל֮ אֲשֵׁמִ֣ים׀אֲנַחְנוּ֮ עַל־אָחִינוּ֒ אֲשֶׁ֨ר רָאִ֜ינוּ צָרַ֥ת נַפְשׁ֛וֹ בְּהִתְחַֽנְנ֥וֹ אֵלֵ֖ינוּ וְלֹ֣א שָׁמָ֑עְנוּ עַל־כֵּן֙ בָּ֣אָה אֵלֵ֔ינוּ הַצָּרָ֖ה הַזֹּֽאת׃
records.gloss: And they said each to his brother, truly guilty we [are] concerning our brother, whose distress of soul we saw when he pleaded with us, and we did not listen; therefore has come upon us this distress.
pieces: They said to each other, "We really are guilty over what we did to our brother. We watched his anguish as he begged us for mercy, and we refused to listen. Now this same anguish has come down on us."

L.21: And they said to one another, "Truly we are guilty concerning our brother, in that we saw the distress of his soul when he pleaded with us, and we did not listen. That is why this distress has come upon us."

R.21: The brothers said to one another, "We are guilty for what we did to our brother. He was so afraid, and he begged us to have mercy, but we paid no attention. Now the same kind of trouble has come on us."

decisions.choice: truly guilty: bearing the guilt of a wrong
decisions.reason: Ashem means to be guilty and to carry the consequences of guilt. The brothers see their trouble as payment for an old sin.

decisions.choice: distress for distress: the punishment fits the deed
decisions.reason: The same word, tsarah, describes Joseph's anguish then and theirs now. Chapter 37 did not tell us that Joseph pleaded with them from the pit; we learn it here, from their own confession.

records.source: וַיַּעַן֩ רְאוּבֵ֨ן אֹתָ֜ם לֵאמֹ֗ר הֲלוֹא֩ אָמַ֨רְתִּי אֲלֵיכֶ֧ם׀לֵאמֹ֛ר אַל־תֶּחֶטְא֥וּ בַיֶּ֖לֶד וְלֹ֣א שְׁמַעְתֶּ֑ם וְגַם־דָּמ֖וֹ הִנֵּ֥ה נִדְרָֽשׁ׃
records.gloss: And answered Reuben them, saying, did I not say to you, saying, do not sin against the boy? And you did not listen; and also his blood, behold, is required.
pieces: Reuben broke in, "I told you, did I not, not to harm the boy? You would not hear of it. And now his blood is being demanded back from us."

L.22: And Reuben answered them, saying, "Did I not tell you, 'Do not sin against the boy'? But you would not listen. And now, look, his blood is required."

R.22: Reuben said to them, "Did I not tell you not to harm the boy? You refused to listen. Now we are being made to pay for his death."

decisions.choice: his blood is required: we must answer for his life
decisions.reason: God "requires" (darash) the blood of anyone who sheds human blood (9:5-6). Reuben believes Joseph is dead and that God is now calling them to account.

decisions.choice: do not sin against the boy: Reuben's earlier plea
decisions.reason: In 37:21-22 Reuben told them not to kill Joseph. His words here put his plea more sharply than that account did.

records.source: וְהֵם֙ לֹ֣א יָֽדְע֔וּ כִּ֥י שֹׁמֵ֖עַ יוֹסֵ֑ף כִּ֥י הַמֵּלִ֖יץ בֵּינֹתָֽם׃
records.gloss: And they not knew that was hearing Joseph, for the interpreter [was] between them.
pieces: They had no idea that Joseph understood them, since he had been speaking to them through an interpreter.

L.23: And they did not know that Joseph understood, for there was an interpreter between them.

R.23: The brothers did not know that Joseph could understand what they were saying. Joseph had been talking to them through a man who translated for him.

decisions.choice: hearing: understanding
decisions.reason: Shama, "hear", here means understand a language (11:7).

decisions.choice: the interpreter: a go-between at court
decisions.reason: Melits is one who speaks between two parties. A high Egyptian official would speak to foreigners through such a man, and Joseph keeps up the pretense that he knows no Hebrew.

records.source: וַיִּסֹּ֥ב מֵֽעֲלֵיהֶ֖ם וַיֵּ֑בְךְּ וַיָּ֤שָׁב אֲלֵהֶם֙ וַיְדַבֵּ֣ר אֲלֵהֶ֔ם וַיִּקַּ֤ח מֵֽאִתָּם֙ אֶת־שִׁמְע֔וֹן וַיֶּאֱסֹ֥ר אֹת֖וֹ לְעֵינֵיהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And he turned away from them and wept; and he returned to them and spoke to them, and he took from them Simeon and bound him before their eyes.
pieces: Joseph stepped away from them and wept. When he came back, he talked with them again, then picked out Simeon and had him tied up right in front of them.

L.24: And he turned away from them and wept. Then he returned to them and spoke to them, and he took Simeon from them and bound him before their eyes.

R.24: Joseph went away from them and cried. When he returned, he spoke with them again. Then he took Simeon and had him tied up as the others looked on.

decisions.choice: he wept: the first of Joseph's tears over his brothers
decisions.reason: Hearing their confession, Joseph weeps in secret. He weeps again at the sight of Benjamin (43:30), and openly when he makes himself known (45:2, 14-15).

decisions.choice: Simeon: the next oldest after Reuben
decisions.reason: Reuben, the eldest, had tried to save Joseph, as Joseph has just heard (verse 22), so Joseph takes the second son. Simeon had also led the violence at Shechem (34:25). The text gives no reason.

records.source: וַיְצַ֣ו יוֹסֵ֗ף וַיְמַלְא֣וּ אֶת־כְּלֵיהֶם֮ בָּר֒ וּלְהָשִׁ֤יב כַּסְפֵּיהֶם֙ אִ֣ישׁ אֶל־שַׂקּ֔וֹ וְלָתֵ֥ת לָהֶ֛ם צֵדָ֖ה לַדָּ֑רֶךְ וַיַּ֥עַשׂ לָהֶ֖ם כֵּֽן׃
records.gloss: And commanded Joseph, and they filled their containers [with] grain, and to return their silver, each to his sack, and to give them provisions for the journey; and it was done for them thus.
pieces: Joseph ordered his men to fill the brothers' containers with grain, to slip each man's money back into his sack, and to give them food for the road. They did all this for them.

L.25: Then Joseph gave orders, and they filled their containers [with] grain, and [he ordered them] to put back each man's silver in his sack, and to give them provisions for the journey. And this was done for them.

R.25: Joseph told his men to fill the brothers' bags with grain. He also told them to put each brother's money back in his bag and to give them food for the trip. His men did all this.

decisions.choice: silver: the payment for the grain
decisions.reason: Kesef is the metal silver, weighed out as payment; there were no coins yet. The word runs through chapters 42-44.

decisions.choice: their silver returned: a gift that looks like a trap
decisions.reason: Joseph's purpose is not stated. To the brothers, who once sold Joseph for silver (37:28), finding the silver brings terror rather than relief (verses 28, 35).

decisions.choice: money
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "silver"; Balanced and Readable say "money" because the silver is the price paid for grain, as in chapter 44.

decisions.choice: his men
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "they filled"; those who carried out Joseph's orders are named.

records.source: וַיִּשְׂא֥וּ אֶת־שִׁבְרָ֖ם עַל־חֲמֹרֵיהֶ֑ם וַיֵּלְכ֖וּ מִשָּֽׁם׃
records.gloss: And they lifted their grain on their donkeys and went from there.
pieces: They loaded the grain onto their donkeys and set off.

L.26: And they loaded their grain on their donkeys and went away from there.

R.26: The brothers loaded the grain on their donkeys and went on their way.

records.source: וַיִּפְתַּ֨ח הָאֶחָ֜ד אֶת־שַׂקּ֗וֹ לָתֵ֥ת מִסְפּ֛וֹא לַחֲמֹר֖וֹ בַּמָּל֑וֹן וַיַּרְא֙ אֶת־כַּסְפּ֔וֹ וְהִנֵּה־ה֖וּא בְּפִ֥י אַמְתַּחְתּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And opened the one his sack to give fodder to his donkey at the lodging place, and he saw his silver, and behold, it [was] in [the] mouth of his sack.
pieces: When they stopped for the night, one of them opened his sack to feed his donkey and saw his money lying at the top of the sack.

L.27: And as one [of them] opened his sack to give his donkey fodder at the lodging place, he saw his silver, and look, it was in the mouth of his sack.

R.27: That night, where they stopped to rest, one of the brothers opened his bag to get food for his donkey. There was his money at the top of the bag!

decisions.choice: the lodging place: a stopping place for the night
decisions.reason: Malon is simply a place to spend the night on a journey, likely a campsite by the road, not a building.

decisions.choice: sack (amtachat): a grain bag
decisions.reason: Two words are used for the brothers' bags, saq ("sack") and amtachat, a word found only in chapters 42-44. They seem to mean the same bags.

decisions.choice: at the top of the sack
alternatives: in the mouth of his sack
decisions.reason: The "mouth" of a sack is its opening; the money lay just inside it.

records.source: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֶל־אֶחָיו֙ הוּשַׁ֣ב כַּסְפִּ֔י וְגַ֖ם הִנֵּ֣ה בְאַמְתַּחְתִּ֑י וַיֵּצֵ֣א לִבָּ֗ם וַיֶּֽחֶרְד֞וּ אִ֤ישׁ אֶל־אָחִיו֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר מַה־זֹּ֛את עָשָׂ֥ה אֱלֹהִ֖ים לָֽנוּ׃
records.gloss: And he said to his brothers, has been returned my silver, and also, behold, [it is] in my sack. And went out their heart, and they trembled each to his brother, saying, what [is] this God has done to us?
pieces: He called to his brothers, "Someone has given my money back! Look, it is right here in my sack!" Their courage failed them. They turned to one another, shaking, and asked, "What has God done to us?"

L.28: And he said to his brothers, "My silver has been returned; look, it is right in my sack!" And their hearts went out [of them], and they turned trembling to one another, saying, "What is this that God has done to us?"

R.28: He told his brothers, "My money has been given back! It is here in my bag!" The brothers were terrified. Shaking with fear, they said to each other, "What has God done to us?"

decisions.choice: their heart went out: their courage failed
decisions.reason: The heart "going out" pictures losing heart in sudden fear.

decisions.choice: what has God done to us?: conscience sees God's hand
decisions.reason: Having just confessed their guilt (verse 21), the brothers read the returned silver as God's doing. It is the first time in the story that they mention God.

records.source: וַיָּבֹ֛אוּ אֶל־יַעֲקֹ֥ב אֲבִיהֶ֖ם אַ֣רְצָה כְּנָ֑עַן וַיַּגִּ֣ידוּ ל֔וֹ אֵ֛ת כָּל־הַקֹּרֹ֥ת אֹתָ֖ם לֵאמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: And they came to Jacob their father, to [the] land of Canaan, and told him all the [things] happening to them, saying,
pieces: Back home with their father Jacob in the land of Canaan, they gave him a full account of all that had happened to them.

L.29: And they came to Jacob their father in the land of Canaan, and they told him all that had happened to them, saying,

R.29: Back in Canaan, the brothers went to their father Jacob and told him the whole story. They said,

records.source: דִּ֠בֶּר הָאִ֨ישׁ אֲדֹנֵ֥י הָאָ֛רֶץ אִתָּ֖נוּ קָשׁ֑וֹת וַיִּתֵּ֣ן אֹתָ֔נוּ כִּֽמְרַגְּלִ֖ים אֶת־הָאָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: Spoke the man, the lord of the land, with us harsh [things], and he took us as spying out the land.
pieces: "The man who rules that country was harsh with us. He accused us of coming to spy out the land.

L.30: "The man, the lord of the land, spoke harshly with us and took us for men spying out the land.

R.30: "The man who rules Egypt spoke roughly to us. He said we were spies.

decisions.choice: the lord of the land: the plural of majesty
decisions.reason: Adoney is plural in form, "lords of", used of a single person of high rank to express his greatness (also verse 33).

records.source: וַנֹּ֥אמֶר אֵלָ֖יו כֵּנִ֣ים אֲנָ֑חְנוּ לֹ֥א הָיִ֖ינוּ מְרַגְּלִֽים׃
records.gloss: And we said to him, honest we [are]; not are we spies.
pieces: We told him, 'We are honest. We are no spies.

L.31: But we said to him, 'We are honest [men]; we are not spies.

R.31: But we told him, 'We are honest. We have not come to spy.

records.source: שְׁנֵים־עָשָׂ֥ר אֲנַ֛חְנוּ אַחִ֖ים בְּנֵ֣י אָבִ֑ינוּ הָאֶחָ֣ד אֵינֶ֔נּוּ וְהַקָּטֹ֥ן הַיּ֛וֹם אֶת־אָבִ֖ינוּ בְּאֶ֥רֶץ כְּנָֽעַן׃
records.gloss: Twelve we [are], brothers, sons of our father; the one is not, and the youngest today [is] with our father in [the] land of Canaan.
pieces: There were twelve of us brothers, all sons of one father. One is gone, and the youngest is at home with our father in Canaan right now.'

L.32: We are twelve brothers, sons of our father. One is no more, and the youngest is with our father today in the land of Canaan.'

R.32: There are twelve of us, all with the same father. One of us is gone. The youngest stayed with our father in Canaan.'

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלֵ֗ינוּ הָאִישׁ֙ אֲדֹנֵ֣י הָאָ֔רֶץ בְּזֹ֣את אֵדַ֔ע כִּ֥י כֵנִ֖ים אַתֶּ֑ם אֲחִיכֶ֤ם הָֽאֶחָד֙ הַנִּ֣יחוּ אִתִּ֔י וְאֶת־רַעֲב֥וֹן בָּתֵּיכֶ֖ם קְח֥וּ וָלֵֽכוּ׃
records.gloss: And said to us the man, the lord of the land, by this I will know that honest you [are]: your brother, one, leave with me, and [for] the hunger of your households take and go.
pieces: Then the man, the ruler of the land, told us, 'This is how I will know you are honest. One of your brothers stays here with me; the rest of you take what your hungry families need and go.

L.33: Then the man, the lord of the land, said to us, 'By this I will know that you are honest [men]: leave one of your brothers with me, and take [grain for] the hunger of your households, and go.

R.33: Then the ruler of Egypt told us, 'I will find out if you are honest. One of your brothers must stay here with me. The rest of you take food home to your hungry families.

records.source: וְ֠הָבִיאוּ אֶת־אֲחִיכֶ֣ם הַקָּטֹן֮ אֵלַי֒ וְאֵֽדְעָ֗ה כִּ֣י לֹ֤א מְרַגְּלִים֙ אַתֶּ֔ם כִּ֥י כֵנִ֖ים אַתֶּ֑ם אֶת־אֲחִיכֶם֙ אֶתֵּ֣ן לָכֶ֔ם וְאֶת־הָאָ֖רֶץ תִּסְחָֽרוּ׃
records.gloss: And bring your brother, the youngest, to me, that I may know that not spies you [are], that honest you [are]; your brother I will give to you, and the land you may go about in.
pieces: And bring me your youngest brother; then I will be sure you are honest men and no spies. I will hand your brother back to you, and you may move about the country and do business.'"

L.34: And bring your youngest brother to me. Then I will know that you are not spies but honest [men]. I will give your brother [back] to you, and you may trade in the land.'"

R.34: Bring your youngest brother back with you. That will prove you are honest and are not spies. I will return your brother to you, and you will be free to buy and sell in this land.'"

decisions.choice: go about in the land: travel and trade freely
decisions.reason: Sachar means to go about as a trader (34:10, 21). Joseph did not mention trade in verse 20; the brothers' report adds it.

decisions.choice: the brothers' retelling softens the story
decisions.reason: In telling their father, the brothers leave out the three days in prison and Joseph's threat of death (verses 17, 20), and add the promise of free trade. They try to spare Jacob, or to persuade him to send Benjamin.

records.source: וַיְהִ֗י הֵ֚ם מְרִיקִ֣ים שַׂקֵּיהֶ֔ם וְהִנֵּה־אִ֥ישׁ צְרוֹר־כַּסְפּ֖וֹ בְּשַׂקּ֑וֹ וַיִּרְא֞וּ אֶת־צְרֹר֧וֹת כַּסְפֵּיהֶ֛ם הֵ֥מָּה וַאֲבִיהֶ֖ם וַיִּירָֽאוּ׃
records.gloss: And it was, they [were] emptying their sacks, and behold, each man's bundle of silver [was] in his sack; and they saw their bundles of silver, they and their father, and they were afraid.
pieces: Then they began emptying their sacks, and in each man's sack lay his purse of money. When they and their father saw the purses, fear came over them.

L.35: And as they were emptying their sacks, look, each man's bundle of silver [was] in his sack! And when they and their father saw their bundles of silver, they were afraid.

R.35: When the brothers emptied their bags, each man found his money, still tied up in its pouch, inside his grain bag. When they and their father saw the money, they were afraid.

decisions.choice: bundle: a pouch tied shut
decisions.reason: Tseror is a small bag or bundle tied up with a cord, used to carry silver (Proverbs 7:20).

decisions.choice: the money found twice: at the lodging place and at home
alternatives: a second account of the same discovery
decisions.reason: In verse 27 one brother finds his silver on the way; here all of them find theirs at home, in front of their father. Perhaps only one sack was opened on the road, or the story tells the discovery from two angles. Either way the fear grows.

records.source: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֲלֵהֶם֙ יַעֲקֹ֣ב אֲבִיהֶ֔ם אֹתִ֖י שִׁכַּלְתֶּ֑ם יוֹסֵ֤ף אֵינֶ֨נּוּ֙ וְשִׁמְע֣וֹן אֵינֶ֔נּוּ וְאֶת־בִּנְיָמִ֣ן תִּקָּ֔חוּ עָלַ֖י הָי֥וּ כֻלָּֽנָה׃
records.gloss: And said to them Jacob their father, me you have bereaved; Joseph is not, and Simeon is not, and Benjamin you will take; upon me are all of them.
pieces: Their father Jacob said to them, "You are leaving me childless! Joseph is no more, Simeon is no more, and now you would take Benjamin from me too. All of it lands on me!"

L.36: And Jacob their father said to them, "You have bereaved me [of my children]: Joseph is no more, and Simeon is no more, and you would take Benjamin. All these things have come upon me!"

R.36: Their father Jacob said to them, "You are taking my children from me! First Joseph was lost, then Simeon. And now you plan to take Benjamin away as well. All these troubles fall on me!"

decisions.choice: bereaved: robbed of children
decisions.reason: Shikkel means to make someone childless. Jacob blames his sons, more truly than he knows: they did take Joseph from him.

decisions.choice: upon me are all these: I bear it all
alternatives: all these things are against me
decisions.reason: Jacob feels every loss falls on him alone. The words can also be heard as "all this is against me".

records.source: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר רְאוּבֵן֙ אֶל־אָבִ֣יו לֵאמֹ֔ר אֶת־שְׁנֵ֤י בָנַי֙ תָּמִ֔ית אִם־לֹ֥א אֲבִיאֶ֖נּוּ אֵלֶ֑יךָ תְּנָ֤ה אֹתוֹ֙ עַל־יָדִ֔י וַאֲנִ֖י אֲשִׁיבֶ֥נּוּ אֵלֶֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: And said Reuben to his father, saying, my two sons you may kill if not I bring him to you; put him in my hand, and I will bring him back to you.
pieces: Reuben told his father, "If I do not bring him home to you, you can kill my own two sons. Leave him in my charge, and I will see that he comes back to you."

L.37: Then Reuben said to his father, "You may put my two sons to death if I do not bring him [back] to you. Put him in my hand, and I will bring him back to you."

R.37: Reuben told his father, "Trust me with Benjamin, and I will bring him home to you. If I fail, you may put my two sons to death."

decisions.choice: my two sons you may kill: a rash pledge
decisions.reason: Reuben offers two of his own sons (he had four, 46:9) as a pledge for Benjamin. The offer is wild: the death of two grandsons could hardly comfort Jacob. Judah's later pledge of himself (43:9) succeeds where this fails.

decisions.choice: Benjamin
decisions.reason: Readable names Benjamin for clarity.

records.source: וַיֹּ֕אמֶר לֹֽא־יֵרֵ֥ד בְּנִ֖י עִמָּכֶ֑ם כִּֽי־אָחִ֨יו מֵ֜ת וְה֧וּא לְבַדּ֣וֹ נִשְׁאָ֗ר וּקְרָאָ֤הוּ אָסוֹן֙ בַּדֶּ֨רֶךְ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר תֵּֽלְכוּ־בָ֔הּ וְהוֹרַדְתֶּ֧ם אֶת־שֵׂיבָתִ֛י בְּיָג֖וֹן שְׁאֽוֹלָה׃
records.gloss: And he said, not will go down my son with you, for his brother is dead, and he alone is left; and [if] befalls him harm on the way which you go on it, you will bring down my gray hair in sorrow to Sheol.
pieces: But Jacob said, "My son will not go down with you. His brother is dead, and he alone remains. If anything happened to him on your journey, you would bring me, gray-haired, down to the grave in grief."

L.38: But he said, "My son shall not go down with you, for his brother is dead, and he alone is left. If harm comes to him on the journey you are going on, you will bring down my gray hair in sorrow to Sheol."

R.38: But Jacob answered, "My son is staying here. His brother is dead, and he is all I have left. If something bad happens to him on the trip, I will die of sorrow. You will send me, an old man, to my grave."

decisions.choice: he alone is left: the only son of Rachel
decisions.reason: Jacob means Benjamin is the only son of Rachel still living (44:20, 27), but he says it to ten other sons standing before him.

decisions.choice: bring down my gray hair: cause an old man's death
decisions.reason: Gray hair stands for old age; to bring it down to Sheol is to bring an old man to his death (44:29, 31).

decisions.choice: Sheol: the place of the dead
decisions.reason: Sheol is the Hebrew name for the realm of the dead, pictured as below the earth, where all go at death (37:35).

decisions.choice: the grave
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew name Sheol; Balanced and Readable say "the grave", what the phrase means here.

decisions.choice: I will die of sorrow. You will send me, an old man, to my grave.
alternatives: you will bring down my gray hair in sorrow to Sheol
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of gray hair going down to Sheol, as in 44:29.
